verses.text: This is the family tree of Jesus the Messiah, descendant of David and Abraham.
Abraham had Isaac; Isaac had Jacob; Jacob had Judah and his siblings.
Judah had Perez and Zerah with Tamar; Perez had Hezron; Hezron had Ram.
Ram had Amminadab; Amminadab had Nahshon; Nahshon had Salmon.
Salmon had Boaz with Rahab; Boaz had Obed with Ruth; Obed had Jesse.
Jesse had David the king; David had Solomon with the wife of Uriah.
Solomon had Rehoboam; Rehoboam had Abijah; Abijah had Asa.
Asa had Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat had Joram; Joram had Uzziah.
Uzziah had Jotham; Jotham had Ahaz; Ahaz had Hezekiah.
Hezekiah had Manasseh; Manasseh had Amon; Amon had Josiah.
Josiah had Jeconiah and his siblings during the Babylonian exile.
After the exile, Jeconiah had Shealtiel; Shealtiel had Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel had Abiud; Abiud had Eliakim; Eliakim had Azor.
Azor had Zadok; Zadok had Achim; Achim had Eliud.
Eliud had Eleazar; Eleazar had Matthan; Matthan had Jacob.
Jacob had Joseph, Mary’s husband, from whom Jesus was born, the Messiah.
From Abraham to David were fourteen generations, from David to the exile fourteen generations, and from the exile to the Messiah fourteen generations.
Here’s how Jesus was born: Mary, engaged to Joseph, was pregnant through the Holy Spirit before they lived together.
Joseph, a just man, didn’t want to make her look bad publicly, so he planned to separate quietly.
But while he was thinking, an angel appeared in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, don’t stress about taking Mary as your wife. The child is from the Holy Spirit.
She will have a son. Call him Jesus because he will save his people from their sins.”
This happened to fulfill what the Lord spoke through the prophet:
“A virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel”—meaning “God with us.”
Joseph woke and did as the angel told him; he married Mary.
He didn’t have relations with her until she gave birth to her firstborn son, and he named him Jesus.
When Jesus was born in Bethlehem during King Herod’s reign, some wise men from the East pulled up in Jerusalem.
They said, “Where’s the newborn King of the Jews? We saw His star shine and came to honor Him.”
When King Herod heard this, he got stressed, and the whole city felt the tension too.
He gathered the chief priests and scribes and asked them where the Messiah was supposed to show up.
They told him, “In Bethlehem of Judea — the prophecy already said it.”
“Because the prophet wrote, ‘Bethlehem, you’re not the least; out of you will come a leader who’ll guide My people Israel.’”
Then Herod secretly called the wise men and asked them exactly when the star appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Search carefully for the child. When you find Him, let me know so I can honor Him too.”
After hearing the king, they left, and the same star they saw in the East went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star stop, they were filled with joy — heavy joy.
They entered the house, saw the child with Mary His mother, bowed down, and honored Him. Then they opened their treasures and gave Him gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
God warned them in a dream not to return to Herod, so they headed back to their country using another route.
After they left, an angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Get up. Take the child and His mother and go to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, because Herod is looking to destroy the child.”
Joseph got up, took the child and His mother that night, and left for Egypt.
They stayed there until Herod died. This fulfilled what the Lord said through the prophet: “Out of Egypt have I called My Son.”

When Herod realized the wise men didn’t return, he got furious. He sent orders and killed all the boys two years old and under in Bethlehem and the surrounding area, based on the time he learned from the wise men.
Then the prophecy spoken by Jeremiah was fulfilled:
“A voice was heard in Ramah — deep crying and grief; Rachel weeping for her children and not willing to be comforted, because they are gone.”
After Herod died, an angel appeared again to Joseph in a dream in Egypt.
The angel said, “Get up. Take the child and His mother and return to Israel, because the ones who wanted the child gone are dead.”
Joseph got up, took the child and His mother, and went back to Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was ruling in Judea instead of his father Herod, he became afraid. God warned him in a dream again, so he turned aside into the region of Galilee.
He settled in a city called Nazareth. This fulfilled what the prophets said — that He would be called a Nazarene.
In those days, John the Baptist popped out in the wilderness, preaching like, “Yo, pull up and repent.”
“The kingdom of heaven is literally right here — lock in.”
He’s the one Isaiah was talking about: “A voice in the wild saying, ‘Prep the path for the Lord — straighten the road.’”
John had that wilderness aesthetic — camel-hair fit with a leather belt, living on locusts and wild honey. Dude’s lifestyle was raw and fully dedicated, no flexing, just mission.
People from Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole area around Jordan were going out to him.
They confessed their sins and John baptized them in the Jordan River — full reset mode.
When he saw the Pharisees and Sadducees pulling up to his baptism, he was like, “Brood of snakes, who warned y’all about the wrath loading?”
“If you’re serious, show real fruit — not fake repentance vibes.”
“And don’t start saying, ‘We’re Abraham’s kids.’ God can raise children for Abraham out of these random stones. Don’t play.”
“The axe is already at the trees. Any tree not producing good fruit? It’s getting chopped and tossed into the fire. No idle vibes.”
“I’m baptizing you with water for repentance, but Someone way more powerful is coming. I’m not even worthy to handle His sandals. He’ll baptize you with the Holy Ghost and fire — real upgrade.”
“His winnowing fan is in His hand — He’s clearing the floor, gathering the good grain, and the trash is getting burned. No recycling.”
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to get baptized by John.
John tried to stop Him, saying, “Bro, I need *You* to baptize *me* — and You’re coming to me?”
Jesus told him, “Let it happen now. This is the proper way for us to carry out everything God requires.” So John agreed and baptized Him.
When Jesus got baptized, He came out of the water, and the heavens literally opened. The Spirit of God came down on Him like a dove — real divine flex.
And a voice from heaven said, “This is My beloved Son, and I’m pleased with Him.” Heavenly stamp of approval.
Jesus got led by the Spirit into the wilderness to face the devil’s tests.
He fasted 40 days and nights. Afterward, He was hungry.
The tempter rolled up: “If You’re the Son of God, turn these stones into bread.”
Jesus clapped back: “It’s written: Humans don’t live on bread alone, but on every word from God.”
Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the temple’s top.
“If You’re the Son of God, jump down — it’s written God will send His angels to catch You.”
Jesus replied: “It’s also written, ‘Don’t test the Lord your God.’”
The devil then took Him to a super high mountain and showed all the kingdoms and their glory.
“I’ll give You all this if You bow and worship me.”
Jesus said: “Go away, Satan. Worship the Lord your God only.”
The devil left, and angels came to serve and support Jesus.
When Jesus heard John got locked up, He moved into Galilee.
Leaving Nazareth, He settled in Capernaum by the sea, in Zebulun and Naphtali’s area.
This fulfilled Isaiah’s prophecy:
“Land of Zebulun and Naphtali, along the sea, past the Jordan, Galilee of the nations —”
“People living in darkness saw a great light; those in death’s shadow got light.”
From then, Jesus began preaching: “Repent. Heaven’s kingdom is here.”
Walking by the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon (Peter) and Andrew, throwing nets.
He said: “Follow Me, I’ll make you fishers of people.”
They left their nets immediately and followed Him.
Going on, He saw two more brothers, James and John, with their father Zebedee fixing nets.
He called them, and they immediately left the boat and their father to follow Him.
Jesus went all over Galilee, teaching in synagogues, preaching the kingdom’s gospel, and healing every sickness and disease.
His fame spread through all Syria. People brought everyone sick, possessed, epileptic, or paralyzed to Him, and He healed them.
Great crowds followed Him from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.
Jesus saw the crowds, went up on a mountain, and sat down. His disciples rolled up close.
He started teaching:
“Blessed are the humble in spirit — they’re squad with heaven’s kingdom.”
“Blessed are those who mourn — comfort is coming their way.”
“Blessed are the chill and meek — they’ll inherit the earth.”
“Blessed are those who crave God’s righteousness — they’ll be fully satisfied.”
“Blessed are the merciful — mercy will bounce back to you.”
“Blessed are the pure in heart — they’ll see God face to face.”
“Blessed are the peacemakers — they’ll get called God’s own squad.”
“Blessed are those who get persecuted for standing for what’s right — heaven’s kingdom is theirs.”
“Blessed are you when people roast you, lie about you, or hate on you for My name.”
“Rejoice and hype up — your reward in heaven is massive. Prophets got the same treatment.”
“You are the salt of the earth — if salt loses its flavor, it’s trash. Can’t season anything anymore.”
“You are the light of the world — a city on a hill can’t be hidden.”
“No one lights a lamp just to hide it under a basket. They put it on a stand so it shines for everyone.”
“Let your glow flex before people, so they see your good deeds and give props to your Father in heaven.”
“Don’t think I came to cancel the Law or the Prophets — I came to fulfill them.”
“Truly, until heaven and earth pass, not one letter or stroke of the Law will disappear until it’s done.”
“Whoever breaks even the smallest command and teaches others to do so will be called least in the kingdom. Whoever keeps and teaches them will be called great.”
“Your righteousness has to out-level the Pharisees and teachers of the law — or you won’t enter heaven’s kingdom.”
“You heard it said: ‘Do not murder. Whoever murders will be judged.’”
“But I tell you, anyone angry with their brother without a cause will be judged. Anyone who calls them ‘bruh’ or ‘clown’ will face real consequences.”
“If you bring your gift to the altar and remember your brother has beef with you,”
“leave your gift there. Go settle it first, then come back and offer your gift.”
“Settle with your adversary quickly while on the way, or they might hand you to the judge, and you’ll end up in jail.”
“You won’t get out until you’ve paid the last penny.”
“You heard: ‘Do not commit adultery.’”
“But I tell you, anyone who looks at someone lustfully has already committed adultery in their heart.”
“If your right eye makes you sin, pluck it out. Better to lose one part than your whole body thrown into hell.”
“If your right hand makes you sin, cut it off. Better to lose one part than your whole body in hell.”
“It was said: ‘Whoever divorces, let him give a certificate.’”
“But I tell you, anyone who divorces except for sexual immorality makes their spouse an adulterer; whoever marries a divorced person commits adultery.”
“Again, you heard: ‘Do not break your oath, but keep vows to God.’”
“But I tell you, don’t swear at all — not by heaven, God’s throne,”
“nor by earth, His footstool, nor by Jerusalem, the city of the great King,”
“nor by your head — you can’t change a single hair’s color.”
“Let your word be straight yes or no. Anything extra is from evil.”
“You heard: ‘Eye for eye, tooth for tooth.’”
“But I tell you, don’t resist evil. If someone slaps your right cheek, turn the other too.”
“If someone wants to sue you for your shirt, give your coat too.”
“If someone forces you to go a mile, go two.”
“Give to anyone who asks, and don’t turn away the one who wants to borrow.”
“You heard: ‘Love your neighbor, hate your enemy.’”
“But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who mistreat you.”
“Then you’ll be children of your Father in heaven. He makes the sun rise on good and evil, sends rain on just and unjust.”
“If you only love those who love you, what’s the reward? Even tax collectors do that.”
“If you only greet your brothers, what’s special? Even Gentiles do that.”
“Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.”
“Yo, don’t do your good deeds to flex for humans — if you do, you already got your reward.”
“When you give to the needy, don’t broadcast it like a clout chase. They got their reward already.”
“Give in secret. Your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.”
“For real, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.”
“When you pray, don’t be like the fake influencers praying in public to get noticed. They got their reward.”
“Pray in private, behind closed doors — your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
“Don’t babble like pagans, thinking more words = He’ll listen.”
“Your Father already knows what you need before you ask.”

“So pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, your name stay holy. Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth like it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our debts, like we forgive our debtors. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.’”
“For yours is the kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.”
“If you forgive others, your Father will forgive you.”
“But if you don’t forgive, your Father won’t forgive your debts either.”
“When you fast, don’t act sad or dramatic like hypocrites. They already got their reward.”
“No, when you fast, wash your face, put oil on your head — keep it private. Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
“Don’t stack treasures on earth where moths and rust destroy, and thieves break in and steal.”
“Stack treasures in heaven instead — safe from all loss.”
“Where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.”
“Your eyes are like a lamp for your body. If your eyes are good, your whole body is full of light.”
“But if your eyes are bad, your whole body is full of darkness. If the light inside you is darkness, how deep is that darkness?”
“No one can serve two bosses. You’ll hate one and love the other. You can’t serve both God and money.”
“So I tell you, don’t stress about your life — what you’ll eat or drink — or about your body — what you’ll wear.”
“Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothes?”
“Look at the birds: they don’t plant, harvest, or store, but your Father feeds them. Aren’t you more valuable?”
“Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to your life?”
“And why stress about clothes? Look at the lilies of the field: they don’t work or spin thread.”
“Even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed like one of these.”
“If God clothes the grass, which is here today and thrown in the fire tomorrow, won’t He take care of you, little faith fam?”
“So don’t worry, asking, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’”
“All the pagans chase these things — your Father knows you need them.”
“Seek first His kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things will get added to you.”
“So don’t stress about tomorrow. Tomorrow has its own worries; today has enough stress of its own.”
“Therefore, don’t worry about what you’ll eat or drink.”
“Don’t worry about clothes either.”
“See the lilies of the field. Even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed like one. If God clothes the grass, He’ll take care of you. Chill and trust Him.”
“Don’t judge others, or you’ll get judged the same way.”
“The way you measure others is the way it’ll be measured back to you.”
“Why you pointing out the speck in your friend’s eye, but ignoring the log in your own?”
“Hypocrite! Take the log outta your own eye first, then you can help your friend with their speck.”
“Don’t throw shade while you’re blind to your own faults. Handle your stuff first, then you can help.”
“Don’t feed holy things to people who will just roast them. Don’t waste what’s sacred on haters.”
“Ask, and it’ll be given to you. Seek, and you’ll find. Knock, and doors open.”
“For everyone who asks gets, everyone who seeks finds, and to everyone who knocks, doors open.”
“Which parent would give their kid a stone when they ask for bread?”
“Or give a snake when they ask for fish?”
“If you, being flawed, know how to give good gifts to your kids, your Father in heaven gives even better to those who ask Him.”
“So treat others how you want to be treated — that’s the essence of the Law and Prophets.”
“Enter through the narrow gate. The wide gate leads to destruction and a packed road, many going that way.”
“The narrow gate is harder, but it leads to life — few find it.”
“Watch out for fake prophets — they come dressed nice, but inside they’re wolves.”
“You’ll know them by their actions. Grapes from thorns? Nah. Figs from thistles? Nah.”
“Every good tree makes good fruit; every bad tree makes bad fruit.”
“A bad tree can’t make good fruit, and a good tree can’t make bad fruit.”
“Every tree not making good fruit is cut down and thrown in the fire.”
“So, you’ll know them by their actions.”
“Not everyone who calls me ‘Lord’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does my Father’s will.”
“Many will say on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy, cast out demons, and do miracles in Your name?’”
“Then I’ll tell them straight: ‘I never knew you. Get lost, you doers of evil.’”
“So whoever hears my words and does them is like a wise builder, building on rock.”
“Rain, floods, winds hit, but the house stands because it’s on rock.”
“But whoever hears and doesn’t do is like a dumb builder, building on sand.”
“Rain, floods, winds hit — house collapses, total L.”
“Jesus finished these teachings, and the crowd was shook — amazed at his authority, not like the Pharisees.”
Jesus came down the mountain, and a dude with leprosy rolled up to him.
He said, ‘Lord, if you’re willing, you can make me clean.’
Jesus reached out, touched him, and said, ‘You’re clean.’ Immediately, leprosy bounced.
Jesus said, ‘Don’t flex this yet. Go show yourself to the priest and offer what Moses commanded for proof.’
Jesus rolled into Capernaum, and a Roman officer came to him saying, ‘Lord, my homie is bed-bound, paralyzed, hurting big time.’
Jesus said, ‘I’ll come and heal him.’
The officer clapped back, ‘Nah, Lord. I’m not worthy for you to step in my crib. Just say the word, and my dude’s healed.’
‘For I know authority. Even my soldiers obey me.’
Jesus was like, ‘Bet, I haven’t seen faith like this in Israel!’
Jesus told the officer, ‘Go — it’s done for you like you believed.’ The dude got healed that hour.
Jesus told the crowd, ‘Many will come from east and west and eat in the kingdom of heaven with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’
‘But the children of the kingdom? Kicked out into the darkness where there’s weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
Jesus healed many who were sick, demon-possessed, paralyzed, or lame.
He came to Peter’s house. Peter’s mother-in-law had a fever.
Jesus touched her hand, fever bounced, and she got up and started serving them.
When evening rolled in, they brought all the sick and demon-possessed to him.
He healed everyone, fulfilling Isaiah’s prophecy: ‘He took our pain and bore our suffering.’
Seeing the crowd, Jesus gave a serious vibe: ‘Y’all, following me isn’t casual.’
A disciple said, ‘Lord, I’ll roll with you anywhere.’
Jesus said, ‘Foxes got dens and birds got nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.’
Another said, ‘Lord, let me go bury my dad first.’
Jesus said, ‘Follow me, and don’t get distracted by the dead burying the dead.’
Jesus got in a boat with his disciples.
A huge storm hit the sea, and waves were crashing on the boat. Jesus was asleep.
The disciples woke him up, saying, ‘Lord, save us! We’re about to drown!’
Jesus said, ‘Chill.’ He rebuked the winds and the sea, and instantly it was calm.
The disciples were shook, saying, ‘Yo, who is this? Even the wind and waves obey him!’
When they got to the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men came from the tombs, super violent, nobody could pass that way.
They screamed, ‘Jesus, Son of God, what you want with us? Don’t torture us before time.’
Far off, a herd of pigs was feeding. The demons begged, ‘Send us into them.’
Jesus said yes, and the demons bounced into the pigs. The herd ran off a cliff into the sea — total wipeout.
The herdsmen ran to the city and told everyone what happened, especially what happened to the demon-possessed men.
The whole city came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
The formerly demon-possessed men stayed in the city, telling everyone what Jesus did for them.
Jesus rolled up in a boat, came back to His hometown, lowkey moving in.
Some dudes brought a paralytic on a stretcher. They couldn’t get close, so they got creative.
Jesus saw their faith and said, “Fam, your sins are forgiven.”
Some scribes were lowkey shady, thinking, “Bruh, this is blasphemy.”
Jesus clapped back, “Why you thinking like that in your head?”
“Which is easier: to say your sins are forgiven, or to say ‘get up and walk’?”
But to show I got receipts, check this: get up, take your stretcher, and bounce to your crib.
Everyone peeped it and were shook, glorifying God—they said, “We’ve never seen faith like this.”
Jesus rolled past, saw Matthew chilling at the tax booth. “Yo, roll with me,” He said. Matthew bounced up.
Matthew hosted a big feast at his crib. Loads of sinners and homies came through.
The Pharisees side-eyed, “Yo, why you eating with these clout-chasing sinners?”
Jesus said, “Nah, healthy peeps don’t need a doc, sick ones do. Lowkey I came to call sinners, not the perfect squad.”
Then John’s crew slid in: “Why your squad doesn’t fast?”
Jesus said, “Yo, when the bridegroom’s here, you don’t mourn. Fasting comes later.”
“Nobody patches old drip with new thread, that’s a mess. Old wineskins? New wine? Nah, they pop.”
While He was talking, a leader rolled up: “My daughter just died. Come bless her.”
Jesus bounced with him, crowd trailing.
On the way, a lady with chronic bleeding slid in, thinking, “If I just touch His fit, I’m gucci.”
She touched Him lowkey, and immediately the blood flow stopped.
Jesus felt power leave Him, and was like, “Who touched me?”
The disciples were like, “Bro, the crowd’s huge. Chill.”
Jesus scanned, saw her, “Don’t worry, little faith fam. You’re healed.”
While talking, a house sent word: “Your daughter’s dead. Don’t stress the walk.”
Jesus said, “Nah, don’t fear, just believe.”
He rolled in, held her hand, and she got up.
Everyone shook and hype: “This is insane.”
Two blind men caught up. “Yo, Jesus, mercy!”
He asked, “Do you believe I can fix this?”
They said, “Yup, fam.”
He clapped back, “Bet,” touched their eyes.
Their vision popped instantly. Jesus told them, “Keep it on the low, no flexing.”
Some dudes brought a mute demon-possessed guy.
Jesus expelled the demon, and the mute spoke. Crowd was shook.
News about Him spread hard across all the hood.
Jesus rolled through all towns and villages, teaching, preaching the kingdom, healing every sickness.
Seeing the crowds, He lowkey felt for them—they were lost, tired, like sheep with no shepherd.
He said to His squad, “Yo, the harvest is crazy big, but the workers? Super few.”
“Pray to the Boss to send more workers, so the harvest doesn’t flop.”
Jesus called His squad of twelve and gave them mad authority over unclean spirits and sicknesses.
The twelve were: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,
Thomas, Matthew, James (Alpha son of Alpha), Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas Iscariot (the one who clapped back later).
Jesus sent them out, commanding them: “Don’t roll with the Gentiles or Samaritans for now, just Israel.”
“Go straight to God’s lost sheep in Israel.”
“Don’t take detours, keep it real.”
“Preach: ‘The kingdom of heaven is here—get woke.’”
Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, kick out demons. Free moves, no payment needed.
Don’t bring cash, wallet, shoes, or extra fits. Travel light.
Don’t have backup squad for the road, no double crew. Rely on God.
Roll up to a house, stay there until you bounce. Don’t hop around.
Greet the house with peace.
If the peeps there are chill, your peace sticks; if not, it bounces back.
Anyone who ignores you? Shake it off like dust from your feet—messengers of God ain’t stressed by haters.
Lowkey, anyone rejecting you in a city? That city is gonna feel the heat on Judgment Day.
Watch yourself: I’m sending you out like lambs in the wolves’ den.
Stay woke, fam. They’ll drag you to councils and churches for My name.
You’ll be judged and dragged before leaders, prophets, kings… all for Me.
Don’t sweat it when they snitch on you. I got your back; My Spirit will drop the right words.
You won’t be on mute. Speak bold when the time comes.
Family might betray you—dad, mom, bro, sis, even your own squad. Some will cancel you for Me.
Haters will even try to kill you, but if you hold strong, you’re gucci.
Bounce out of one city when they hate you, and hit the next. You won’t finish the mission before hitting all the towns of Israel.
Don’t think you’re above your Master. The student follows the Master’s path.
A disciple isn’t above the teacher; they’re family and aligned.
Don’t get shook. The truth will out; God sees all.
Speak loud, let the world hear. Don’t lowkey hide what I’m dropping.
Fear no human squad. Fear God who can end the soul and body forever.
God notices even the sparrows, bro. Not one dies without His nod.
Your hairs? Counted. Don’t stress the details He’s got.
You’re worth more than all the birds combined. God’s got you.
Everyone who flexes Me before humans, I’ll flex them before God.
Anyone who denies Me in front of humans? I’ll deny them before the Big Boss.
Don’t think I came to bring peace only. I came to stir up, even against family sometimes.
I bring the truth and realignment. Sword energy, not chill vibes.
Some will clash with dad, mom, bro, sis, in-laws—faith over blood ties.
Anyone loving fam over Me? Can’t be My disciple.
Anyone picking their own life over Me? Can’t be My disciple.
Whoever saves their life to play it safe? Will lose it.
Whoever rolls with Me and My message? Will find life, the real, eternal plug.
Give a prophet a vibe check? You get prophet-tier rewards.
Give a disciple a nod? You get disciple-tier rewards. Even a simple cup of water to a little one for My name? You’re stacked.
Jesus dipped out and started schooling His squad, sending them out with instructions.
John, locked up in jail, heard what Jesus was doing and sent word: “Yo, are You the real deal, or should we wait for someone else?”
Jesus replied: “Go tell John what you see: blind peeps see, lame walk, lepers get clean, deaf hear, dead get resurrected, poor get the Kingdom plug.”
“Blessed is anyone who doesn’t ghost on Me over this.”
When John bounced, Jesus started dropping wisdom for the crowd.
“Blessed are the peeps who don’t get shook by Me.”
He started throwing facts about John: “What did you go out to see? A hype man in silk? Nah. Those who flex with silk live the high life, not John.”
“Did you go for a party dude? Nah, John’s all about the Word. He’s the prophet of fire, the voice in the desert: make the path clear for God.”
“Everyone tries to call him small, but even the least in God’s kingdom is bigger than him.”
“He’s the messenger you’ve been waiting for; it’s written in prophecy: ‘I send My messenger ahead of You to prep the way.’”
“Real talk, no one born of woman is bigger than John—but the smallest in God’s kingdom? They flex bigger than him.”
“Kingdom energy is being chased by violence. Violent seekers grab it—grind hard to get in.”
“The Law and the Prophets ran till John. If you feelin’ me, read the vibes—God’s been schooling the squad since day one.”
“If you’ve got eyes to see, John’s Elijah energy is here—he’s the one the prophets said would pop up.”
“Anyone with ears, listen up, no cap.”
“But for the new gen? The squad’s acting childish—complaining no matter what. I played tunes, you didn’t dance; I sang sad songs, you didn’t cry.”
“John came fasting, not hype, and they said he’s possessed. I came eating, kicking it, and they called Me a party dude, a glutton. Smh.”
“Wisdom flexes in her children, and the crowd shows who’s tuned in.”
Jesus started calling out the cities that ghosted Him despite all the signs. “Yo, Chorazin, Bethsaida—y’all got mad miracles, but y’all didn’t humble up.”
“If Tyre and Sidon had seen these vibes, they’d be on their knees rocking sackcloth and ashes.”
“But y’all? Nah. Judgment is heavier on you than them.”
“Capernaum, yo—you’re the plug town for Me, but you act wild, so you get hit harder than the OG cities.”
“You’ll get ghosted by judgment if you don’t humble up, fam.”
Jesus flipped to gratitude mode: “Big ups to You, God, Father of heaven and earth. You keep it lowkey from the smart and hype, and reveal to the humble fam.”
